controls.title: Use approved cryptographic algorithms
controls.statement: Select approved algorithms, protocols, cipher suites and key sizes for each cryptographic use and remove disallowed choices.
controls.risk: Weak or obsolete cryptography could allow protected information or transactions to be read, changed or forged.
controls.scope: Cryptographic uses in applications, services, network protocols, stored data and authentication systems.
controls.examine: Compare the cryptographic inventory and technical configurations with the approved algorithm, protocol, strength and key-size requirements for each use.
controls.interview: Ask security architects how approved choices are set, updated and communicated when standards or threats change.
controls.test: Inspect or negotiate representative cryptographic connections and operations and verify that disallowed algorithms and cipher suites are rejected.
test_steps: Select representative data stores, network services, applications, certificates and protocols and identify the approved algorithm and strength requirements for each.
Inspect effective configuration and perform an authorised negotiation or cryptographic operation to confirm approved algorithms and key sizes are selected.
Attempt negotiation with prohibited, deprecated or undersized options and verify rejection without silent downgrade.
Compare discovered use with the cryptographic inventory and record undocumented exceptions, expiry dates and dependencies that prevent migration.
controls.expected: Every sampled use applies an approved algorithm and strength for its purpose, and disallowed choices cannot be selected.

mappings.basis: States approval status for symmetric algorithms, including disallowed two-key TDEA; other algorithm classes require their own table checks.
Requires AES-GCM for encryption of TLS connections in its stated scope.
Requires the organisation to determine cryptographic uses and implement the cryptography required for them.

controls.title: Manage cryptographic keys through their lifecycle
controls.statement: Generate, store, distribute, rotate, revoke and destroy cryptographic keys using approved methods and defined cryptoperiods.
controls.risk: Compromised, poorly generated or overused keys could expose protected information and make trusted identities or transactions unreliable.
controls.scope: Cryptographic keys and secrets from generation through archival or destruction.
controls.examine: Inspect key inventories, generation records, protection controls, cryptoperiods, rotation and revocation records, and destruction evidence.
controls.interview: Ask key custodians how key lifetimes are chosen, how compromise is handled and how duties are separated.
controls.test: Sample active and retired keys and trace their creation, storage, use, rotation or revocation and final disposition.
test_steps: Sample active, recently rotated, revoked, expired and destroyed encryption and signing keys from different services.
Trace each key through authorised generation, ownership, protected storage, distribution, permitted use, backup or escrow and scheduled rotation.
Perform an authorised rotation or revocation in a test service and verify the new key works, the old key cannot authorise new activity and dependent systems update safely.
Inspect destruction or retirement evidence and confirm retained keys remain available only where required for lawful decryption, verification or recovery.
controls.expected: Keys are generated with approved cryptography, protected throughout use and retired within the applicable cryptoperiod or immediately after compromise.

mappings.basis: Provides suggested cryptoperiods by key type; lifecycle controls beyond the period require separate evidence.
Requires keys used by authenticators to be generated using approved cryptography.
Requires key-management infrastructure covering generation, storage, destruction, update and revocation.
